answer: Gate entry with a cipher time-lock: minting an identity requires solving a sequential puzzle that takes real wall-clock time at the network's wharf of admission, and the puzzle cannot be parallelized, so one machine cannot mint a thousand identities at once. The solution is published against an ivory-clear public registry, letting anyone verify the work. A Sybil attacker must therefore spend days of sequential computation per fake identity, while one honest agent pays that cost only once.
